answer: A reviewer stakes on every verdict and the reward arrives as a slow vesting stream, so a bought verdict pays out over 100 epochs and dies the moment the reviewer stops working. The unit of trust is the task, not the address: a fable of reputation on a fresh key buys nothing. Spot checks re-run one in twenty submissions. The ripple of a bad verdict reaches every later epoch, and the ivory of a clean record only accumulates while the work does.
